title: How Startodel works
body:
# How Startodel works

Startodel is a personal developer learning platform. Call `get_guide` first. Use the learner’s goals to build a Track, teach a Lesson, ask for practice, assess the answer and revisit due Topics. The MCP Token selects the Owner on every request. Omit User and Owner IDs from all Tool arguments. The external agent judges free-text Exercises and Grill Questions from actual answers and records the evidence. Startodel scores multiple-choice Quizzes and schedules reviews.

The Profile holds the Onboarding Questionnaire. Each Topic lives once in the Owner’s Topic Catalog. Its stable Topic Slug identifies it across Tracks. A TopicEdge points from prerequisite to dependent. A Track orders memberships and can carry Track Sources. Its Lessons, Mastery and ReviewItems follow their Topics wherever those Topics appear.

A Lesson contains ordered Blocks. A Quiz Attempt stores the choices and score at submission. Lesson Progress records reading. Mastery records demonstrated depth. A GrillSession holds ordered questions, answers, their Answer Source and the agent’s Verdicts. Use `get_progress` for an overview before planning another round.

title: Complete the Onboarding Questionnaire
body:
# Complete the Onboarding Questionnaire

Once connected, call `get_guide` first, then `get_profile` to see which questionnaire answers are missing. Ask about the learner’s stack, goals and grade, and save their answers with `update_profile`.

To connect, have the learner sign in, issue a personal MCP Token in Settings and configure a Streamable HTTP client for the installation’s `/mcp` URL. Store the token in the client’s secret input and send it as a Bearer credential on each request.

Save partial answers as they arrive. Stack and goals are lists of strings. Save grade in `experience` as junior, middle, senior or lead. After the learner confirms the questionnaire is complete, send `markOnboarded: true` and call `get_guide` again.

title: Working with the learner
body:
# Working with the learner

The learner signs in to the web app to manage MCP Tokens and see their Profile and Tracks. They describe a goal to their external agent, agree on a Track outline and choose a Topic to study. Ask whether they want an explanation, an Exercise or a GrillSession.

Present a Lesson in chat when needed. Mark it read with `mark_lesson_read` after the learner confirms reading it. Record their chosen Quiz options with `record_quiz_result`. For a spoken or typed Grill answer in chat, use `submit_grill_answer`. If a UI client has already submitted an answer, read it with `get_grill` and judge that stored answer directly. Both paths use the same history.

title: Choose the next Topic
body:
# Choose the next Topic

Use `get_progress`, `list_tracks` and `get_track_graph` to choose a Topic with Mastery below 2 whose prerequisites have reached level 2. Inspect `get_topic` and `list_lessons` before creating content.

Use the learner’s goal to select among eligible Topics. Check prerequisites across the Topic Catalog, including those outside the current Track. When a graph has no eligible Topic, check for an unmet external prerequisite, a cycle or a completed Track. Use `get_lesson` to teach existing material. Ask the learner to apply it and keep an example of their work as evidence for `set_mastery`. Call `get_guide` again after each round.

title: Build a Track around a technology
body:
# Build a Track around a technology

Agree on a concrete outcome, then use `create_track`, `upsert_topics`, `add_edges` and `attach_topics_to_track` to build a small first Track Graph.

For a goal like diagnosing slow queries, work backward from a query plan to scans, indexes and cardinality estimates. Search `list_topics` by slug prefix for reusable Topics. Batch up to 100 Topics and keep the returned IDs by slug. Add up to 200 directed prerequisite edges per call. Put the selected slugs in teaching order. Attaching puts these Topics first and keeps the remaining members in their previous order. Repeating the same order preserves membership and positions.

Read the graph back with `get_track_graph`. Use `remove_edge` to correct a prerequisite, `detach_topic_from_track` to remove a membership and `update_track` to revise the description or sources. Confirm large changes with the learner. Detaching a Topic preserves its Lessons.

title: Build a Track from a repository
body:
# Build a Track from a repository

Ask for the repository, the target revision or release and a task the learner wants to perform. Read the README, dependency manifest, relevant source entry points, tests and documentation for that revision. Follow one real call from public API to implementation.

Use `create_track` with an ordinary Track title, a description naming the revision, and Track Sources such as `{"repo":"https://github.com/vuejs/core","docs":["https://vuejs.org/guide/introduction.html"]}`. Read it back with `get_track`. Distinguish public behavior from internals in the Lessons. Tie version-specific features to a tag, release note or source permalink. Ask for access or a public reference when evidence is missing.

Find reusable Topics by slug with `list_topics`, then use `upsert_topics` for the Topics the task requires. Add prerequisite-to-dependent edges with `add_edges`, attach the selected slugs in teaching order with `attach_topics_to_track` and verify the result with `get_track_graph`. Keep repository-specific internals under a stable slug and point each Lesson at the code and tests supporting it.

title: Write a Lesson with Blocks
Continue a GrillSession
body:
# Continue a GrillSession

Use `list_grills` and `get_grill` to resume an open GrillSession. Choose prompts with `get_grill_candidates`, save them with `add_grill_questions`, capture chat answers with `submit_grill_answer` and assess them with `judge_grill_answer`. Close the round with `finish_grill`.

Use `start_grill` for a new round. The default target is 15 questions. A Track limits candidates to its members. Due ReviewItems come first, oldest first, followed by the weakest Topics. Select prompts that test recall, application and explanation. Attach each question to its Topic when possible. Add up to 30 questions in one call. Ask one at a time and wait for the learner’s own answer.

Give a strong Verdict for a correct answer that explains the mechanism or applies it accurately. Give partial for a sound core idea with an important missing condition. Give weak for an incorrect mechanism or an inability to apply it. Quote the specific part of the answer that informed the Verdict, explain one correction and offer a follow-up. Partial and weak Verdicts refresh a linked Topic’s ReviewItem. Finishing returns Verdict counts and weak Topics. Previously submitted answers can still be judged after finishing.

The learner can submit answers on the Grills page. Call `get_grill` to find answers with Answer Source `ui` and no Verdict. Pass each stored answer’s question ID to `judge_grill_answer` with specific feedback. The learner can refresh the question to see that judgment.

title: Review due Topics
body:
# Review due Topics

Call `list_due_reviews`, ask the learner to recall or apply each Topic, then pass the assessed Verdict and a short reason to `record_review_result`. Use `set_mastery` when the evidence supports a change in depth.

A new ReviewItem starts in box 0. Strong advances one box up to 4, partial stays in the current box and weak resets to box 0. From the time of assessment, the resulting boxes 0 through 4 schedule the next review in 1, 3, 7, 16 and 35 elapsed days respectively. A weak Grill answer schedules tomorrow. Record a standalone review once. Judging a weak or partial Grill answer already schedules its linked Topic.

Mastery 0 means “don’t know.” The platform raises Mastery from 0 to 1 when every Lesson is read, and to 2 when every Quiz has a fully correct latest Quiz Attempt. Each rule requires at least one Lesson or Quiz respectively. Reading and Quiz results never lower Mastery. Use `set_mastery` with concrete evidence for level 3 when the learner explains why something works, or 4 when they can trace the internals. These levels belong to the external agent.

The Reviews page offers a Practice Quiz when the Topic contains Quiz Blocks. Submitting it records the Quiz Attempts and schedules the next ReviewItem automatically. Check the current ReviewItem before arranging another review.

title: Rules for external agents
body:
# Rules for external agents

When unsure what to do next, call `get_guide` first. The MCP Token selects the Owner. Never pass User or Owner IDs to a Tool.

Use the learner’s own answers and confirmed facts. Ask for missing information. Never invent User data, answers, Quiz Attempts, evidence or Verdicts. Ask before a large rewrite of a Track Graph or Lesson, especially when a Topic appears in multiple Tracks.

Keep Topic Slugs and Block IDs stable. Review the existing graph and content before writing. Treat missing records as unavailable in this Owner’s catalog. Keep credentials, repository secrets and private keys out of prompts, Profiles, Track Sources, Lessons and logs. Direct the learner to the app to revoke a lost MCP Token.

Tracks start private. Never publish or unpublish unless the user explicitly asked in this conversation. Use `set_track_visibility` with the Track ID and requested visibility. Publishing requires the learner to accept the current Publishing rules and Terms of Use in the app. If acceptance is missing, ask the learner to open the Track and publish there once.

A Public Track shares its sources, member Topics and their Lessons. The public Lesson preview hides Quiz answers and Exercise solutions. Forking creates a private, editable copy with working practice, including those answers and solutions. Learning activity stays with its Owner. Consider all Public Tracks containing a Topic before editing a shared Lesson.
